subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored `/exec` session defaults be allowed to relax or override later operator `tools.exec` config, or should operator config become a security floor for all resumed sessions?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but current docs and tests intentionally describe persistent `/exec` session defaults, so automation should not choose the security precedence and migration policy on its own.

options.title: Make config a security floor
options.body: Treat global or per-agent `tools.exec` policy as the minimum security boundary, allow session defaults only when they do not relax it, and add reset or migration coverage for stored entries.

options.title: Keep session persistence as authoritative
options.body: Document that authorized `/exec` defaults intentionally persist across config changes and add an operator-facing reset or audit path so admins can clear stale session fields.

options.title: Version and expire session exec defaults
options.body: Track the config generation used when `/exec` defaults were stored and clear or re-evaluate them after relevant `tools.exec` changes.

recommendation.title: Make config a security floor
recommendation.body: Treat global or per-agent `tools.exec` policy as the minimum security boundary, allow session defaults only when they do not relax it, and add reset or migration coverage for stored entries.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the `/exec` session override behavior and is the strongest current-history owner for the resolver, persistence, and docs surface.
